prompt: What is the lowest DUI test result at which an Arizona driver 21 or older loses the driving privilege on the spot?
explanation: If a DUI test shows an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more, you lose your driving privilege on the spot. 0.15 is the threshold for Extreme DUI, not the basic limit.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 65

prompt: What is the alcohol concentration limit in Arizona for someone driving a commercial vehicle that requires a CDL?
explanation: The limit is 0.04 in a commercial vehicle requiring a commercial driver license, half of the 0.08 limit for other adult drivers.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 65

prompt: A 19-year-old Arizona driver has a small amount of alcohol in their system, well below 0.08. What can happen?
choices: Their license may be suspended, because drivers under 21 may not have any alcohol concentration
They receive a warning only, since it is a first offense
Nothing, because they are under the 0.08 limit
Nothing, unless they test at 0.05 or higher
explanation: Arizona is Under 21 = Zero Tolerance. If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if there is any alcohol concentration.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 65

prompt: Under Arizona's Implied Consent Law, what happens the first time you refuse a test after a DUI arrest?
choices: You automatically lose your driving privilege for 12 months
Nothing, as long as you agree to a test in court later
You lose your driving privilege for 90 days
You lose your driving privilege for 30 days
explanation: Refusing or failing to complete a test after a DUI arrest means automatic loss of your driving privilege for 12 months (24 months for a second refusal within 84 months).
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 65

prompt: An Arizona driver refuses a DUI test for the second time within 84 months. How long is the driving privilege lost?
explanation: A second refusal within 84 months (7 years) costs you your driving privilege for 24 months, double the 12-month penalty for a first refusal.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 65

prompt: For a first standard DUI conviction in Arizona, what is the minimum jail time?
explanation: A first DUI brings at least 10 consecutive days in jail. 30 days is the minimum for a first Extreme DUI, and 90 days for a second DUI.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 66

prompt: For a first standard DUI conviction in Arizona, the driver license is suspended for at least how long?
explanation: A first DUI means a license suspension of not less than 90 days, plus jail, a fine of at least $1,250, alcohol screening/education/treatment and community service.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 66

prompt: In Arizona, "Extreme DUI" applies starting at what alcohol concentration?
explanation: Extreme DUI applies to an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or higher. At 0.20 or higher the minimum jail time increases further.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 66

prompt: A first-time offender is convicted of Extreme DUI with a 0.16 alcohol concentration. What minimum jail time applies?
explanation: A first Extreme DUI (0.15 or higher) means at least 30 consecutive days in jail and a fine of at least $2,500. The 45-day minimum applies at 0.20 or higher.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 66

prompt: Which situation makes a DUI an Aggravated DUI in Arizona?
choices: Driving under the influence with a passenger under 15 in the vehicle
Driving under the influence with an alcohol concentration of 0.09
Driving under the influence for the first time
Driving under the influence at night
explanation: Aggravated DUI covers a DUI while suspended or revoked, a third DUI in 7 years, a DUI with a person under 15 in the vehicle, or a DUI while required to use an ignition interlock.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 66

prompt: Under Arizona's open container law, where may an open container of alcohol be legally carried in a car that has a trunk?
choices: In a cup holder if a passenger holds it
explanation: The passenger compartment, where open containers are illegal, includes any unlocked compartments or portable devices within reach of the driver or passengers. It does not include the trunk.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 59

prompt: Which phone use is legal for an Arizona driver while driving?
choices: Holding the phone to your ear for a short call
Using the phone hands-free or with voice-to-text
Recording a video if the phone is in your hand
Reading a text while driving slowly
explanation: Arizona law prohibits holding or supporting a wireless device while driving. Hands-free and voice-to-text use is allowed.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 24

prompt: Arizona law allows a driver to hold and use a wireless device while driving in only one situation. What is it?
choices: To check a navigation app at low speed
To send a short text in light traffic
To answer a call from a family member
explanation: A wireless device may only be used while driving to report an emergency. Otherwise drivers may not hold or support a device.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 24

prompt: Which of these is prohibited for all Arizona drivers while driving, even if the phone is mounted on the dash?
explanation: Arizona drivers may not write or read text-based messages, and may not watch, record or broadcast video while driving. Hands-free calls and voice-to-text are allowed.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 24

prompt: During the first 6 months with an Arizona graduated (Class G) license, when may a teen use a cell phone while driving?
choices: Any time, if a parent approves
Any time, as long as it is hands-free
Only in an emergency or to operate an audible navigation system
explanation: For the first 6 months, a Class G driver may not use a wireless device while driving except in an emergency or to use an audible turn-by-turn navigation system that is not set or adjusted by hand while driving. Hands-free calls are not an exception.

prompt: Under Arizona's safety belt law, the driver must make sure passengers under what age are buckled up?
explanation: The operator of a motor vehicle must require all passengers under the age of 16 to buckle up.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 19

prompt: Arizona's safety belt law requires which occupants to wear a properly fastened belt while the vehicle is moving?
explanation: Each front-seat occupant must have the lap and shoulder belt (or lap belt, if that is all that is installed) properly adjusted and fastened while the vehicle is in motion. The driver must also require passengers under 16 to buckle up.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 19

prompt: In Arizona, a child under what age must always be secured in a child restraint system?
explanation: Arizona law prohibits transporting a child under five unless the child is properly secured in a child restraint system.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 20

prompt: You are driving a 6-year-old who is 4 feet 5 inches tall in Arizona. What does the law require?
choices: The child must ride in a child restraint system
The child must ride in the front seat with the air bag on
The child may ride unbelted in the back seat
The child may use an adult seat belt alone
explanation: Children between five and eight must be in a child restraint system until they are at least 4 feet 9 inches tall.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 20

prompt: What is the youngest age at which you can get a graduated instruction permit in Arizona?
explanation: You may be issued a graduated and/or motorcycle instruction permit at 15 years and 6 months, after passing the written test. An operator permit requires age 18.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: Who must ride with an Arizona driver who holds a graduated or operator instruction permit?
choices: A parent only, regardless of license status
A licensed driver at least 25, in the back seat
A Class A, B, C or D licensed driver at least 21, seated beside the driver
Any licensed driver 18 or older, seated anywhere in the car
explanation: Permit holders must be accompanied by a Class A, B, C or D licensed driver at least 21 years old who occupies the seat beside them.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: How long must a teen hold an Arizona instruction permit before applying for a graduated license?
explanation: An applicant for a graduated license must have held an Arizona instruction permit for at least 6 months, and it must be valid at the time of application.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 13

prompt: A teen in Arizona skips driver education. How much supervised practice must a parent certify for a graduated license?
choices: At least 20 hours, with no night requirement
At least 40 hours, including 6 at night
At least 30 hours, including at least 10 hours at night
At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
explanation: Without an approved driver education program, a parent or guardian must certify at least 30 hours of supervised practice, including at least 10 hours at night.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 13

prompt: If an Arizona teen completed a Traffic Survival School or Defensive Driving course, how many supervised practice hours must the parent certify?
choices: 20 hours, with at least 6 at night
30 hours, with at least 10 at night
10 hours, with at least 2 at night
explanation: The requirement drops to 20 hours of supervised driving practice, with at least 6 hours at night, if the minor completed a Traffic Survival School or Defensive Driving course.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 13

prompt: What is the minimum age to get a graduated (Class G) driver license in Arizona?
explanation: A graduated driver license is issued to an applicant who is at least 16 but less than 18, after holding a permit for 6 months.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: During the first 6 months with a graduated license, an Arizona teen may not drive during which hours (unless an exception applies)?
explanation: For the first 6 months, a Class G driver may not drive between midnight and 5:00 a.m. unless a licensed parent/guardian is in the front passenger seat or another listed exception applies.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: A 16-year-old with a 2-month-old Arizona graduated license drives alone at 1:00 a.m. Which trip is allowed?
choices: Driving friends home from a movie
Driving directly home from their job
Driving home from a friend's party
Driving to a 24-hour store for snacks
explanation: During the first 6 months, midnight-5 a.m. driving is allowed only with a licensed parent/guardian in the front seat or when driving directly to or from a sanctioned school activity, work, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: During the first 6 months with a graduated license, how many passengers under 18 may an Arizona teen carry (if they are not siblings and no parent is present)?
explanation: A Class G driver may not carry more than one passenger under 18 for the first 6 months, unless the passengers are siblings or a licensed parent/guardian is in the front passenger seat.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: A 16-year-old has held an Arizona graduated license for 3 months and no parent is in the car. Which group of passengers is allowed?
choices: A friend who is 16 and a friend who is 15
Three classmates, if it is daytime
explanation: For the first 6 months, no more than one passenger under 18 is allowed unless the passengers are the teen driver's siblings or a licensed parent/guardian occupies the front passenger seat.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: What is the minimum age to apply for an Arizona operator (Class D) license?
explanation: You must be at least 18 to apply for an operator license. Drivers 16-17 receive a graduated (Class G) license.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 15

prompt: A 17-year-old Arizona graduated licensee is convicted of a first traffic violation. What is the penalty?
choices: They must attend Traffic Survival School
Nothing is recorded for a first violation
explanation: For drivers under 18 with a graduated license, the first traffic conviction requires Traffic Survival School and goes on the driving record. A second brings a 3-month suspension; a third, 6 months.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 13

prompt: What is Arizona's minimum bodily injury liability insurance for injury to one person?
explanation: Arizona's minimums are $25,000 bodily injury for one person, $50,000 for two or more persons, and $15,000 property damage.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 9

prompt: What is the minimum property damage liability coverage required in Arizona?
explanation: Arizona requires $15,000 property damage liability, along with $25,000/$50,000 bodily injury liability.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 9

prompt: An Arizona driver is convicted for the first time of not having proof of insurance. What is the suspension?
choices: 3 months for the license, registration and plates
1 year for the license, registration and plates
There is no suspension for a first violation
explanation: Not having or failing to produce proof of insurance brings a suspension of the license, registration and plates: 3 months for a first violation, 6 months for a second within 36 months, and 1 year for a third or later violation within 36 months.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 64

prompt: How many points within 12 months require an Arizona driver to attend Traffic Survival School or face suspension?
explanation: If you accumulate 8 or more points within any 12-month period, you must attend Traffic Survival School, or your driving privilege may be suspended.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 62

prompt: How many points does a speeding conviction add to an Arizona driving record?
explanation: Speeding is 3 points. Most other moving violations are 2 points; leaving the scene of a crash is 6; DUI and reckless driving are 8.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 63

prompt: Which Arizona violation carries 8 points, enough by itself to require Traffic Survival School?
explanation: DUI, Extreme DUI, Aggravated DUI, reckless driving, racing and aggressive driving are 8 points each. Speeding and gore-area violations are 3; wrong-way driving is 2.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 63

prompt: You move to a new address in Arizona. How soon must you notify MVD?
explanation: Arizona law requires you to notify MVD within 10 days of any change to your name or address.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 6

prompt: You are convicted of running a red light in Arizona. Besides paying the fine, what does MVD require?
explanation: MVD is required by law to order Traffic Survival School for every red-light (or flashing red light) conviction. Points are also assessed, and failing to complete the course means an indefinite suspension.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 38

prompt: To be cited for aggressive driving in Arizona, a driver who creates an immediate hazard must exceed the speed limit and also commit how many other listed violations?
explanation: Aggressive driving means speeding plus two of: failing to obey signs/signals, passing on the right, unsafe lane change, following too close, or failing to yield to emergency vehicles, creating an immediate hazard.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 60

prompt: Arizona state highways have mile posts. About how far apart are they?
explanation: Arizona is one of the few states where all state highways have mileage markers. They are set 2 feet off the right shoulder about 1 mile apart, and help you report your location.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 43

prompt: A vehicle ahead displays the orange-and-red triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem. What is the fastest it can travel?
explanation: A vehicle with the slow-moving vehicle sign cannot travel faster than 25 mph. Slow down; it has the legal right to be on the road.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 52

prompt: In Arizona, what may you do at a curb painted white?
choices: Stop only to load or unload, staying with your car
Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers
explanation: White curb: stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers. Yellow curb: stop only to load or unload and stay with your car. Red curb: no stopping, standing or parking.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 46

prompt: In Arizona, what does a yellow painted curb mean?
choices: You may park there at any time
You may stop only long enough to load or unload, and must stay with your car
You may stop only to pick up or drop off passengers
You may not stop, stand or park
explanation: A yellow curb means you may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 46

prompt: At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal, the overhead lights are flashing red. What should you do?
choices: Slow down and continue without stopping
Stop, then proceed with caution after the pedestrian has finished crossing your half of the road
Stop and wait until the lights go dark
Proceed, because flashing red means the pedestrian has finished crossing
explanation: Flashing red at a pedestrian signal means STOP, then proceed with caution after the pedestrian finishes crossing the driver's half of the roadway.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 36

prompt: In Arizona, when may you cross a solid white line to change lanes?
choices: Only to pass a slower vehicle
When merging into or out of an HOV lane
explanation: A solid white line generally should not be crossed, but vehicles may cross a solid white line when merging into and out of the HOV lane (use your signal and caution).
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 46

prompt: Near a METRO light rail line, how can you tell which way a train is moving?
choices: White headlights mean it is approaching; red taillights mean it is moving away
The front of the train is always painted red
Trains always travel on the right-hand track
A train moving away flashes amber lights
explanation: The ends of a light rail train are identical. White headlights show a train approaching; red taillights show it moving away.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 49

prompt: When following a fire department vehicle responding to an emergency in Arizona, stay at least how far behind it?
explanation: Stay at least 500 feet behind a fire department vehicle and at least 300 feet behind a police vehicle responding to an emergency.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 38

prompt: In Arizona, how far behind a police vehicle responding to an emergency must you stay?
explanation: The required distance is at least 300 feet behind a responding police vehicle (500 feet for a fire department vehicle).
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 38

prompt: Arizona's Move Over Law applies when you pass which stopped vehicles with flashing lights on the side of the road?
choices: Any vehicle, including tow trucks, highway maintenance and private vehicles
explanation: The Move Over Law (A.R.S. 28-775) covers all vehicles pulled over with flashing lights, including emergency, law enforcement, tow trucks, highway maintenance and private vehicles, on freeways, highways and city streets.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 39

prompt: You approach a tow truck with flashing lights stopped on the shoulder, but traffic makes it unsafe to change lanes. What does Arizona law require?
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop completely in your lane until it leaves
explanation: Move over one lane when you can. If it is not safe or possible to move over, you must slow down and use caution.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 39

prompt: In Arizona, you must yield to a funeral procession led by an escort vehicle flashing what color light?
explanation: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to any vehicle in a funeral procession led by a funeral escort vehicle flashing a red or blue light.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 39

prompt: A school bus is stopped with its stop arm out on the other side of a road divided only by painted stripes. You are going the opposite direction. What must you do?
choices: Stop, because painted striping is not a physical divider
Stop only if children are visible
explanation: You may pass in the opposite direction only on a divided roadway with a physical barrier such as a fence, curbing or pavement separation. Roadway striping alone does not count.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 39

prompt: You are on a highway separated by a raised curb median. A school bus with flashing lights and stop arm is stopped on the other side, facing you. What does Arizona law allow?
choices: You may proceed with caution without stopping
You must stop, then proceed at 15 mph
You must stop until the stop arm is pulled in
You must pull onto the shoulder
explanation: On a roadway divided by a physical barrier (fence, curbing or pavement separation), you are not required to stop for a school bus when traveling in the opposite direction. Drive with caution.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 39

prompt: A car in the lane next to you has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian. Your lane is clear and the light is green. What should you do?
choices: Pass carefully since your lane is clear
Pass only if the pedestrian is on the far side
Do not pass the stopped car
explanation: In Arizona you may not pass another vehicle that is stopped for a pedestrian, even if you have a clear lane or a green signal.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 36

prompt: You reach an Arizona roundabout at the same time as a large truck. What should you do?
choices: Pass the truck once you are both inside
Stop inside the roundabout to let it by
Yield to the truck and let it enter first
Enter first, since you are smaller and faster
explanation: Vehicles approaching a roundabout must yield to vehicles already in it and to large vehicles entering at the same time. Do not try to pass large trucks inside the roundabout.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 28

prompt: In Arizona, when may you turn right on a red light?
choices: After a complete stop, when traffic and pedestrians are clear, unless a sign prohibits it
Only when a green arrow is shown
Never; Arizona does not allow right on red
Without stopping, if no cars are coming
explanation: Where not prohibited by signs, a right turn on red may be made after a complete stop, when vehicle and pedestrian traffic are clear.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 34

prompt: In Arizona, in which situation may you turn left on a red light after stopping and yielding?
choices: From any road, if no oncoming traffic is present
From a one-way road onto a two-way road
From a one-way road onto another one-way road
From a two-way road onto a one-way road
explanation: Turning left from a one-way road into a one-way road is the only left turn that may be made against a red light, unless signs prohibit it.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 47

prompt: You are on a one-way street at a red light and want to turn left onto a two-way street. What does Arizona law say?
choices: You may turn only if a pedestrian signal shows WALK
You may turn without stopping if clear
You may turn after stopping and yielding
You must wait for a green light
explanation: A left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road cannot be made against a red light. Only one-way to one-way left turns are allowed on red.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 48

prompt: How far before a turn does Arizona law require you to signal?
explanation: Signal at least 100 feet (about 4 seconds) before you turn so other drivers have time to react.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 26

prompt: You plan to turn into a driveway just past an intersection. According to the Arizona manual, when should you signal?
choices: Once you are in the intersection
You do not need to signal for a driveway
Only after you complete the turn
Well before you reach the intersection
explanation: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal until you are in the intersection, because drivers in the intersection may pull into your path.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 26

prompt: At a Diverging Diamond Interchange (DDI) in Arizona, what is unusual about the cross street?
choices: Traffic must stop at every ramp
Traffic briefly switches to the left side of the road
All turns are made from the center lane
explanation: A DDI briefly moves cross-street traffic to the left side of the roadway. Crossover points occur at signals; follow the signals, signs and pavement markings.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 29

prompt: In Arizona, you must not pass another vehicle when you are within how many feet of a street crossing or railroad crossing?
explanation: Do not pass within 100 feet of a street crossing or railroad crossing, or within 100 feet of a bridge, tunnel or underpass where your view is blocked.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 28

prompt: In an Arizona school crossing zone marked by portable signs, which is true about passing other vehicles?
choices: Passing is allowed if no children are visible
Passing is allowed on the left only
Passing is allowed at 15 mph or less
explanation: Passing another vehicle in a school crossing zone is prohibited, and the maximum speed from the first sign to past the crossing is 15 mph.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 42

prompt: When no limit is posted, what is the speed limit approaching a school crosswalk in Arizona?
explanation: When no limit is posted, the limit is 15 mph approaching a school crosswalk. The 15 mph maximum applies from the first school-crossing sign until past the crossing.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 40

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in an Arizona business or residential district?
explanation: The unposted limit is 25 mph in any business or residential district.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 40

prompt: What is the highest speed limit listed in the Arizona manual, which applies on rural freeways?
explanation: The manual lists 75 mph on rural freeways, the highest Arizona limit. Speed limits vary by road, so always obey the posted signs.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 40

prompt: Portable school-crossing signs are in place on your street. When does the 15 mph school-zone limit end?
choices: After you pass the school crossing
Only when the crossing guard leaves
At the end of the block where the school is
explanation: The maximum speed from the first sign to past the school crossing is 15 mph. When portable signs are not in place, the area's normal speed limit applies.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 42

prompt: What following distance does the Arizona manual recommend for most driving situations?
explanation: Allow at least a 3-second following distance in most situations, and use 3 to 6 seconds when more cushion is needed.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 53

prompt: On a slippery road, the Arizona manual says to increase your following distance to at least how many seconds?
explanation: On slippery roads, double your following distance to 6 seconds or more. In rain, slow down and increase your distance to at least 6 seconds.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 53

prompt: You are driving slower than surrounding traffic on a multi-lane Arizona road. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to the fastest driver's speed
Stay in the left lane so others can see you
Turn on your hazard lights and stay in your lane
Drive in the right lane and let faster vehicles pass
explanation: Driving too slowly can be as dangerous as driving too fast. Keep right and allow faster traffic to pass whenever you are slower than the traffic around you.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 40

prompt: The posted limit is 45 mph, but blowing dust has cut visibility sharply. Under Arizona's basic speed law, how fast may you drive?
choices: 45 mph, since that is the posted limit
No faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Up to 50 mph if traffic is flowing
explanation: A.R.S. 28-701 says you may not drive faster than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and hazards present, and must control speed to avoid a collision.

prompt: In Arizona, you may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
explanation: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 31

prompt: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park in Arizona?
explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 31

prompt: In Arizona, it is illegal to park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. (15 feet is how close you may stop to the nearest track when a train is coming.)
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 31

prompt: Arizona law prohibits parking within how many feet on the approach to a stop sign or traffic signal at the side of the road?
explanation: A.R.S. 28-873 prohibits stopping, standing or parking within 30 feet on the approach to any flashing beacon, stop sign, yield sign or traffic control signal at the side of a roadway.

prompt: How close may you park to the driveway entrance of a fire station in Arizona?
explanation: A.R.S. 28-873 prohibits parking within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance, and within 75 feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the street when posted.

prompt: When parallel parking next to a curb in Arizona, your right-hand wheels must be within how many inches of the curb?
explanation: A.R.S. 28-874 requires parking with the right-hand wheels parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.

prompt: Which of these parking spots is legal in Arizona (if no signs say otherwise)?
choices: Within the boundaries of an intersection
15 feet from a crosswalk at an intersection
explanation: Arizona prohibits parking within an intersection, within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, within 15 feet of a fire hydrant and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. 25 feet from a hydrant is legal.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 31

prompt: What is a gore area on an Arizona freeway?
choices: The HOV lane marked with diamonds
The space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp
explanation: A gore area is the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp. It is against the law to drive over or park in any part of it.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 32

prompt: You are about to miss your exit and could cut across the striped gore area. What is true in Arizona?
choices: It is legal if you signal first
It is illegal only during rush hour
It is legal if no other cars are near
Driving over a gore area is illegal and carries 3 points
explanation: It is against the law to drive over or park in any part of a gore area; the violation carries 3 points. Take the next exit instead.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, pp. 32, 63

prompt: During posted times on weekdays, who may use an Arizona freeway HOV lane?
choices: Vehicles with at least two people (including the driver), motorcycles and buses
Only vehicles with three or more people
Any vehicle, if it travels at the speed limit
explanation: At posted times Monday through Friday, you may not drive a vehicle with fewer than two persons, including the driver, in the HOV lane. Motorcycles and buses may also use it.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 33

prompt: An overhead freeway sign in Arizona reads "ALERT, WRONG-WAY DRIVER AHEAD." What should you do?
choices: Safely move toward the nearest exit as soon as possible
Move into the far left or HOV lane
Stop on the shoulder and wait
Speed up to get past the area quickly
explanation: If you see that message, safely move toward the nearest highway exit as soon as possible. Wrong-way drivers are usually in the left or HOV lane.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 58

prompt: When passing a bicyclist traveling in the same direction, Arizona law requires at least how much space?
explanation: Motorists must allow a minimum safe distance of 3 feet when passing a bicyclist traveling in the same direction.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 50

prompt: You are stopped at a red light on a 40 mph, four-lane Arizona street. A motorcyclist slowly rides past you between the lanes. What is true?
choices: It is always illegal for motorcycles to ride between lanes
It is legal only on freeways
It is legal at any speed
This lane filtering is legal if done safely at 15 mph or less
explanation: Arizona allows motorcycle lane filtering past stopped vehicles on streets with at least 2 lanes in the same direction and a speed limit of 45 mph or less, at no more than 15 mph.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 51

prompt: You are caught in a severe dust storm on an Arizona highway. Where should you stop?
choices: Completely off the highway, as far right as possible
In the emergency lane on the shoulder
In your travel lane with hazard lights on
explanation: Pull Aside, Stay Alive: drive completely off the highway and stop as far right as possible. Do not stop in the travel lane or the emergency lane.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 55

prompt: After pulling off the road in a severe dust storm, what should you do with your lights and brake?
choices: Turn off your lights and take your foot off the brake
Keep your headlights on high beam
Turn on hazard lights and keep your foot on the brake
Keep your low beams on and set the parking brake only
explanation: In a severe dust storm, turn off your lights and take your foot off the brake, stay in the vehicle with seat belts buckled, and wait until the storm passes.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 55

prompt: An Arizona driver goes around a flood barricade and stalls in the water. What can happen?
choices: The state pays for the rescue in all cases
The driver can be billed for the cost of the emergency rescue
Nothing, if no one is hurt
explanation: A driver who drives around barricades set up due to flooding is liable for the expenses of any emergency response needed to remove people from the stalled vehicle.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 56

prompt: Heavy rain has flooded an Arizona wash on your route. What does the manual advise?
choices: Cross if the water looks shallow
Cross quickly before the water rises
Follow the car ahead through the water
Do not cross the flooded wash
explanation: Heavy rain causes flash floods in Arizona washes. Do not cross flooded washes; water can stall your engine, hide potholes and carry your vehicle downstream.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 56

prompt: Arizona law requires headlights during what period?
choices: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
explanation: You must use headlights from sunset to sunrise. Also turn on low beams in sun glare, rain, dust or whenever your vehicle may not be clearly visible.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 57

prompt: In Arizona, when should you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle?
explanation: Use high beams on highways only when no vehicle is coming toward you within 500 feet, and switch to low beams when you meet oncoming traffic.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 57

prompt: When following another vehicle at night in Arizona, use low beams whenever you are within how many feet of it?
explanation: When following another car, use low beams whenever you are within 200 feet.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 57

prompt: What happens to fines for traffic violations in an Arizona work zone where fines-double signs are posted?
explanation: When signs are posted, fines for traffic violations, including speeding, are doubled in Arizona work zones.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 44

prompt: A railroad crossing's lights are flashing and bells are ringing. How close to the nearest track may you stop?
explanation: Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest railroad track when you see flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 42

prompt: You are in a crash in Arizona and someone is injured. Besides staying at the scene and helping, what are you required to do?
choices: Move the injured person to your car
Report it to MVD within 30 days
explanation: Stay at the scene, help the injured and exchange information. In case of injury, you are also required to immediately call the police.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 71

prompt: After a minor, no-injury crash on an Arizona freeway, your car still runs safely. What does state law require?
choices: Drive home and report the crash later
Leave it exactly where it stopped until police arrive
Move it out of the travel lanes
Turn off the engine and wait in the car
explanation: State law requires a driver in a minor crash without injuries to remove an operable vehicle from the roadway if it can be moved safely (Quick Clearance). Never leave the scene.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 71

prompt: If you move your car out of the travel lanes after a minor Arizona crash before police arrive, what is true?
choices: You cannot be held at fault just because you moved it
You must pay a fine for moving it
You lose the right to file an insurance claim
explanation: A person who removes a vehicle from the main traveled roadway before police arrive shall not be held liable or at fault for the crash based solely on moving it.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 71

prompt: In Arizona, failing to stop at a crash that caused a death results in what penalty to the driving privilege?
explanation: Failure to stop: 1-year suspension (vehicle damage only), 3-year revocation (injury), 5-year revocation (serious physical injury), 10-year revocation (death).
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 72

prompt: A driver is convicted of leaving the scene of a crash that only damaged another vehicle. What happens to the Arizona license?
explanation: Conviction for failure to stop at a crash involving only damage to a vehicle results in a 1-year suspension.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 72

prompt: Which motorcycle riders and passengers must wear a protective helmet in Arizona?
explanation: A.R.S. 28-964 requires motorcycle operators and passengers under 18 to wear a protective helmet. The law does not require a helmet for riders 18 and older.

prompt: An adult Arizona motorcyclist rides a bike with no windshield. What eye protection does the law require?
choices: None, because the rider is over 18
Protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield
explanation: All motorcycle operators must wear protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield unless the motorcycle has a protective windshield (A.R.S. 28-964).

prompt: Arizona allows motorcycle lane filtering only on streets with a posted speed limit of no more than what?
explanation: Lane filtering is allowed only where the posted speed limit does not exceed 45 mph and the street has at least 2 adjacent lanes in the same direction.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 51

prompt: When lane filtering in Arizona, a motorcyclist may travel no faster than:
explanation: While filtering past stopped vehicles, the motorcycle may not travel faster than 15 miles per hour.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 51

prompt: In Arizona, which vehicles may a motorcyclist pass by lane filtering?
choices: Vehicles moving slowly in the same direction
Vehicles stopped in the same direction of travel
explanation: Lane filtering means passing a vehicle that is stopped in the same direction and lane, on a street with at least 2 same-direction lanes, a limit of 45 mph or less, at 15 mph or less.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 51

prompt: Which is a restriction on an Arizona motorcycle instruction permit holder?
choices: No passengers and no riding on freeways or interstates
No riding without a licensed adult on the back
explanation: Motorcycle permit holders may not carry passengers, ride on freeways or interstate highways, or ride between sunset and sunrise or whenever light is too poor to see 500 feet.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: How long is an Arizona motorcycle instruction permit valid?
choices: 7 months, renewable only once in a 24-month period
explanation: The motorcycle permit is valid for 7 months and can be renewed only one time within a 24-month period.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 12

prompt: An Arizona applicant under 18 wants a motorcycle license. How long must they have held a motorcycle instruction permit?
explanation: Applicants under 18 must have held an Arizona motorcycle instruction permit for at least six months, and complete an approved course or 30 certified hours of supervised practice. The minimum age is 16.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 15

prompt: Without an approved motorcycle education course, how many hours of supervised motorcycle practice must a parent certify for an Arizona applicant under 18?
explanation: A parent or guardian must certify in writing that the applicant completed at least 30 hours of supervised motorcycle driving practice, unless an MVD-approved motorcycle course was completed.
ref: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, p. 15

prompt: Under Arizona law, how many motorcycles may ride side by side in a single lane?
explanation: A.R.S. 28-903 prohibits operating a motorcycle more than two abreast in a single lane. Motorcycles are entitled to the full use of a lane.
